message.content:
The **Union Square Greenmarket** is widely regarded as the most visited market in New York City. | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Location** | 14th St. & Union Square, Manhattan | | **Operating Days** | Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday (open 8 a.m.–5 p.m.) | | **Annual Foot‑Traffic** | Roughly **1.5 million visitors** per year (estimates from NYC Greenmarket data) | | **Why It Stands Out** | • Largest farmers‑market in NYC by square footage and vendor count.
• Offers a wide variety of fresh produce, artisanal foods, and specialty items.
• Centrally located near major transit hubs (Union Square subway station, several bus lines).
• Hosts seasonal events, cooking demos, and community programs that draw both locals and tourists. | Other notable markets in NYC include: - **Chelsea Market** – a food hall in the Meatpacking District with a mix of restaurants, shops, and pop‑up vendors. - **Grand Central Market** – a smaller, upscale market in Midtown with a curated selection of gourmet foods. - **Brooklyn Flea** – a popular weekend flea market in Williamsburg, known for vintage goods and street food. However, when it comes to sheer visitor numbers and overall popularity, Union Square Greenmarket remains the top choice.
